w: Casa de la Vall was built in 1580 as a fortified manor for the Busquets family and served as the seat of Andorra's General Council until 2011. Its upper floor holds the Council Chamber and the 'closet of the seven keys' - one lock per parish - guarding historic documents. The house appears on Andorra's 1 euro coin.
s: Andorra's parliament house until 2011, on the 1-euro coin

w: Pont de la Margineda has spanned the Gran Valira river in Santa Coloma since the 14th or 15th century. Builders used lightweight pumice for the archstones and granite for the walls, a combination that has kept the medieval bridge standing for over 600 years. It is registered in the Cultural Heritage of Andorra.

_facts: Built in the 14th-15th century
Archstones are pumice for lightness; walls are granite

Registered heritage property of Andorra

n: Esglesia de Sant Marti de la Cortinada
w: Sant Marti de la Cortinada began as a Romanesque church in Ordino parish, then gained Baroque additions during renovations spanning the 17th to 20th centuries. Registered as an asset of cultural interest on 16 July 2003, it mixes two very different architectural eras under one roof.

w: Sant Andreu d'Arinsal, in La Massana parish, was built in the 17th century and still holds an altarpiece of the Virgin Mary from the same period and a 17th-18th-century carving of Saint Andrew. The church is registered in the Cultural Heritage of Andorra, a small stone landmark in the village of Arinsal.

w: Built in the 12th century, Sant Cristofol d'Anyos still carries Romanesque murals of the Last Supper and Saint Christopher. A third mural, of Saints Peter, Paul and Mary, was stolen in the 1930s and stayed missing for nearly a century, resurfacing only in 2023. It was registered as heritage in 2003.

_facts: Built in the 12th century, Romanesque architecture

w: Casa d'Areny-Plandolit is a stone manor house in Ordino, built in 1633. It is registered in the Cultural Heritage of Andorra and now operates as a museum, one of the valley's few surviving 17th-century noble residences open to the public.
s: 1633 manor house-turned-museum of a noble family

n: Parc Natural Comunal de les Valls del Comapedrosa
w: Established in 2003, this national park in western Andorra protects the valleys around Coma Pedrosa, the country's highest peak, near the town of Erts. A moderate public hiking trail takes up to four hours, sometimes with a small fee. The park is being developed under the Ramsar wetlands framework.

_facts: Established in 2003

w: Col de Beixalis crosses the Andorran mountains at 1,795 metres between Anyos and Encamp. Its final stretch was gravel until recently paved, and the climb has twice featured in the Tour de France - stage 9 in 2016 and the summit finish of stage 15 in 2021, when Sepp Kuss led at the top and won.
s: 1,795m pass where Sepp Kuss won a Tour de France stage
_facts: Altitude 1,795m

n: Esglesia de Sant Serni de Nagol
w: Constructed in the 11th century in Sant Julia de Loria parish, Sant Serni de Nagol contains some of the earliest known works of Romanesque art in Andorra. Renovated in the 17th and 18th centuries, it was registered as heritage on 16 July 2003 - a small chapel holding the country's oldest religious paintings.

w: Roca Entravessada rises 2,928 metres on the Pyrenean border between Andorra and Spain. Its Catalan name means 'Rock Askew.' One route to the top climbs from Arinsal past the Estanys Forcats, a chain of mountain lakes, making it a target for hikers based in Andorra's northwest valleys.
